Before Beijing, Michael kept having the same dream.

He'd look up at the scoreboard and see 3:07.

I told him that was probably his 300 split in the 400 IM.

Then in the final, I looked up at the 300 mark and it said 3:07.

He'd seen that race so many times in his head that it already felt familiar to him.

So pick your next big moment and see it clearly, every detail, every day.

There's a distinction I picked up from Kant that changed how I think about money.

Everything you spend on has either a price or a dignity.

Price means it's a means to something else, and it's replaceable. Dignity means it's worth doing for its own sake.

Nobody walks into a gym because they love Bulgarian split squats. Nobody loves Bulgarian split squats. You go because it gets you more years, energy, and mornings on the floor with your kids without you bitching about how much your knees/back/neck hurts

O ritmo de vida em São Paulo pode ter um custo para a saúde. 

Trânsito intenso, horas perdidas no deslocamento, poluição sonora, menos contato com áreas verdes, sedentarismo e estresse fazem parte da rotina de muita gente.

Esses fatores podem contribuir para o risco cardiovascular, especialmente quando se somam a hábitos como dormir pouco e não praticar atividade física regularmente.
